svg.aria-label: Advantages and disadvantages of establishing a partnership compared to remaining a sole trader
svg.text: Why Establish a Partnership? Strategic Gains vs. Real Trade-Offs
When a growing sole trader teams up with partners, resources multiply — alongside shared profits and mutual risk.
✓ 5 Core Reasons to Form a Partnership
1. Larger Capital Pool & Easier Borrowing
Combine savings + assets of 2–20 owners to fund expansion
2. Complementary Skills & Specialization
E.g. Partner A runs sales/design while Partner B runs finance
3. Shared Workload, Holidays & Decision-Making
Business stays open smoothly when one partner is sick/away
4. Shared Business Losses & Risk
Downturns are absorbed across multiple partners, not one person
5. Simple & Private vs. Limited Companies
Low setup cost; financial accounts stay confidential (not public!)
⚠ 5 Key Risks & Disadvantages to Weigh
1. Unlimited Joint & Several Liability
Personal assets of general partners can be seized for firm debts
2. Shared Profits (No Longer 100% Yours)
Profits must be split even if one partner feels they worked harder
3. Risk of Disagreements & Slower Decisions
Clashes over reinvestment, hiring, or Drawings can stall growth
4. Bound by Another Partner's Mistakes
Mutual agency means one partner's bad contract binds ALL partners
5. Instability on Death or Withdrawal
Must revalue assets/goodwill or dissolve if a partner leaves
How Smart Partners Reduce Risks #2, #3 & #5: Sign a Detailed Written PARTNERSHIP AGREEMENT (Lesson 8.3)!
